summary: The dynamic runtime language of the web, Node.js servers, and asynchronous event-driven computing.

rows.means: reassignable variable / immutable binding / legacy function-scoped name
rows.consequence: Always default to const. Use let only when a value must change. Never use var because its hoisting and lack of block scope cause silent bugs.

rows.means: standard function / arrow function with lexical this
rows.consequence: Arrow functions inherit this from their surrounding lexical scope, avoiding the classic .bind(this) bug in object methods and callbacks.

rows.means: prints debug output, error diagnostics, and tabular arrays
rows.consequence: console.table() formats arrays of objects into structured terminal/devtools tables for instant visual inspection.

rows.means: transforms each item into a new array of the same length
rows.consequence: Pure function: never modifies the original array. Returns an entirely new array with the mapped results.

rows.means: returns a new array containing only items passing the test
rows.consequence: Pure function: filters down items where the callback returns a truthy value, omitting everything else.

rows.means: aggregates array items into a single final value or object
rows.consequence: The fundamental array primitive: can build totals, group records by category, or flatten nested hierarchies into a single map.

rows.means: returns the first matching item / returns its array index
rows.consequence: Stops iterating as soon as a match is found (short-circuiting). Returns undefined / -1 if no item matches.

rows.means: checks if value exists (boolean) / returns index of value
rows.consequence: includes() correctly handles NaN comparisons, whereas indexOf() checks strict equality (===) and fails on NaN.

rows.means: checks if at least one item matches / checks if all match
rows.consequence: Short-circuits immediately: some() stops at the first true, every() stops at the first false.

rows.means: non-destructive sub-array copy / destructive in-place mutation
rows.consequence: slice() leaves the original array untouched; splice() deletes or inserts elements directly into the original array.

rows.means: add to end / remove from end / remove from start / add to start
rows.consequence: push/pop are O(1) constant time operations; shift/unshift are O(n) because all remaining array elements must be re-indexed.

rows.means: extracts property names / values / [key, value] tuples
rows.consequence: Object.entries(obj) is ideal for looping over dictionary records using for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj)).

rows.means: unpacks properties or array items directly into distinct names
rows.consequence: Allows setting default values: const { role = 'guest' } = user. Works identically on arrays: const [first, second] = list.

rows.means: shallow copies and merges objects or arrays
rows.consequence: Creates a new shallow copy with immutability, allowing clean state updates without mutating the original reference.

rows.means: strict equality (checks value and type) / loose equality
rows.consequence: Always use ===. Loose equality (==) performs arcane type coercion (e.g. '' == 0 is true, null == undefined is true).

rows.means: deliberate absence of value / variable declared but never assigned
rows.consequence: null is an intentional assignment representing 'empty'; undefined is JavaScript's default for missing parameters or unassigned names.

rows.means: safely accesses nested properties without throwing TypeError
rows.consequence: If any reference in the chain is null or undefined, evaluation stops and safely returns undefined instead of crashing.

rows.means: provides a fallback only when the value is null or undefined
rows.consequence: Falls back only when the left side is null or undefined, unlike the older operator, which also falls back on zero and the empty string — which is the bug it was introduced to fix.

rows.means: writes asynchronous promise code in synchronous style
rows.consequence: Syntax over the same underlying objects: await suspends the function until the pending value settles, so sequential-looking code does not block anything else.

rows.means: represents a future value that hasn't arrived yet
rows.consequence: Can be in one of three states: pending, fulfilled (via resolve(val)), or rejected (via reject(err)).

rows.means: runs promises in parallel; rejects on first error / waits for all
rows.consequence: Promise.all fails immediately if any promise rejects; Promise.allSettled always completes and reports each status individually.

rows.means: native HTTP client for network requests
rows.consequence: Returns a pending value that settles into a response object; the body is read with a second await, because the headers arriving and the body arriving are two different moments.

rows.means: catches and handles runtime exceptions cleanly
rows.consequence: The finally block is guaranteed to run regardless of whether an exception occurred, making it ideal for cleaning up resources.

rows.means: creates and fires a custom runtime exception with stack trace
rows.consequence: Halts the current execution path and bubbles up to the nearest enclosing catch block, preserving the exact line number.

rows.means: finds the first / all matching DOM nodes via CSS selector
rows.consequence: querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList that can be looped over directly with .forEach().

rows.means: binds an event listener to user interactions (click, input)
rows.consequence: Supports options like { once: true } or { passive: true } to optimize mobile touch and scroll performance.

rows.means: manipulates CSS class names on DOM elements safely
rows.consequence: Prevents messy manual string concatenation of className, ensuring classes aren't duplicated or accidentally removed.

rows.means: deserializes text into JS object / serializes JS object to text
rows.consequence: JSON.parse throws SyntaxError on malformed JSON; always wrap in try/catch when reading network or local storage data.

rows.means: persists string key-value pairs across browser sessions
rows.consequence: Stores strings only, so anything structured has to be serialised on the way in and parsed on the way out, and the space available is a few megabytes and varies by browser.

rows.means: schedules a function call after delay / on recurring interval
rows.consequence: Returns a handle that must be kept if the timer is ever to be cancelled, and a repeating timer that nobody cancels keeps the page busy long after the thing that wanted it has gone.

rows.code: class Name extends Base { constructor() { super(); } }
rows.means: object-oriented syntax sugar over prototypal inheritance
rows.consequence: Provides clean constructor initialization, private fields (#privateField), and static methods.

rows.means: collection of unique values / key-value dictionary for any type
rows.consequence: Set guarantees O(1) deduplication; Map allows any data type (including objects or functions) to serve as lookup keys.

rows.means: rounds down / rounds up / rounds to nearest / pseudorandom float
rows.consequence: Math.floor(Math.random() * (max - min + 1)) + min generates an inclusive random integer between min and max.

rows.means: splits text into an array / joins an array into text
rows.consequence: 'a,b,c'.split(',') yields ['a', 'b', 'c']. ['a', 'b'].join('-') yields 'a-b'.

rows.means: removes outer whitespace / replaces pattern matches
rows.consequence: Using a global regex (e.g. /pattern/g) replaces all occurrences, or use modern str.replaceAll().

rows.means: schedules a render update before the browser's next screen repaint
rows.consequence: Synchronizes visual updates with the display refresh rate (typically 60Hz or 120Hz), yielding silky smooth animations.
